source.author: cic
source.text: nam fuit quoddam tempus, cum in agris homines passim bestiarum modo vagabantur et sibi victu fero vitam propagabant nec ratione animi quicquam, sed pleraque viribus corporis administrabant, nondum divinae religionis, non humani officii ratio colebatur, nemo nuptias viderat legitimas, non certos quisquam aspexerat liberos, non, ius aequabile quid utilitatis haberet, acceperat.
source.text_original: nam fuit quoddam tempus, cum in agris homines passim bestiarum modo vagabantur et sibi victu fero vitam propagabant nec ratione animi quicquam, sed pleraque viribus corporis administrabant, nondum divinae religionis, non humani officii ratio colebatur, nemo nuptias viderat legitimas, non certos quisquam aspexerat liberos, non, ius aequabile quid utilitatis haberet, acceperat.
source.text_english: For there was a certain time when men roamed about the fields everywhere like wild beasts and sustained their lives by savage nourishment, and when they managed almost nothing by reason of the mind, but most things by the strength of the body; as yet no regard was paid to divine religion or human duty; no one had seen lawful marriages, no one had recognized legitimate children, and no one had learned what advantage an equitable law might have.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: nam et rudes illi Italiae homines, quos cascos Ennius appellat, qui sibi, ut in Rhetoricis Cicero ait, uictu fero uitam requirebant, ante chartae et membranarum usum aut in dedolatis ex ligno codicellis aut in corticibus arborum mutua epistularum alloquia missitabant; unde et portitores earum tabellarios et scriptores a libris arborum librarios uocauere.
reuse.text_original: nam et rudes illi Italiae homines, quos cascos Ennius appellat, qui sibi, ut in Rhetoricis Cicero ait, uictu fero uitam requirebant, ante chartae et membranarum usum aut in dedolatis ex ligno codicellis aut in corticibus arborum mutua epistularum alloquia missitabant; unde et portitores earum tabellarios et scriptores a libris arborum librarios uocauere.
reuse.text_english: For even those uncultivated men of Italy, whom Ennius calls casci, who, as Cicero says in the Rhetorica, sought out life for themselves by a savage means of living, before the use of paper and parchment used to send mutual messages in letters either on little tablets of wood smoothed down or on the bark of trees; whence they also called the bearers of these messages tabellarii, and the writers librarii, from the books of trees.
